Eskoms cover up : Denton Report

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Why did Eskom try to cover up their own report. We bring you the highlights

Unique Selling Point:
We have all suspected the worst of Eskom, now their own report lifts the lid on the inner workings of this state utility and its not a pretty picture.

Summary:
Its taken Sikonathi Mantshantshe two years to try and find out what was in the Dentons report – a report commissioned by Eskom in 2015 to get to the bottom of what had gone wrong with the state utility. At that stage Eskom didn’t have money to pay salaries, Ingula, Medupi and Kusile were five years late and way over budget, coal costs were soaring and load shedding was a constant problem

Further information:
The Dentons team came in, but very soon found their wings were clipped. They weren’t allowed to see E mails, they could only look at documents at Eskom during office hours, and then when they did present their first interim report, the board decided to collect all the copies and destroy them. Then after only 3 months Eskom closed down their investigation and sent them packing. Meanwhile for two years, at every opportunity he got, Sikonathi kept asking about the Dentons report. The answer from chairman Ben Ngubane was clear, the report he said was not for public consumption. But Sikonathi’s persistence paid off and recently he was leaked the report. Nevertheless on Jan 23rd he asked once more at an Eskom press conference for the report. Eventually eskom agreed but then changed their minds at the last minute. Last week the financial Mail made the entire 304 page report public. It has been sanitized to the point that it cannot be used legally to hold senior executives to account, complains Sikonathi. Nevertheless the report makes for some interesting and hair raising reading and gives insights into just how dysfunctional and corrupt our most critical utility really is and why we our electricity bills have sky rocketed.

Press Release:


Eskom Investigated: The Denton Report
In 2015 the Eskom board commissioned international law firm Dentons to conduct a forensic fact-finding enquiry into the status of the business and the challenges faced by the utility. For two years journalist Sikonathi Mantshantsha pestered Eskom for the report. Chairperson Ben Ngubane told him it was not for public consumption. Last week the Financial Mail released the 300-page report to the South African public. Despite the cover up, the report makes for some explosive reading. Carte Blanche confronts Eskom about why they tried to sanitise and hide their own forensic report.


Script:


Eskom Exposed Final script tx Sunday 26th Feb 2017

Commentary One
Eskom’s coal emergency of 2008, that plunged the country into crisis and damaged the economy, incredibly it now seems, could have been avoided.

Its these, and other revelations revealed in several reports that Deputy Editor of the Financial Mail Sikonathi Mantshantsha has brought to light

Sikonathi Mantshantsha
In 2015 Eskom ran out of money to pay salaries of 50 000 employees! So Eskom had basically collapsed. It took the finance minister at the time, Nhlanhla Nene to hand Eskom R23 billion rand in cash, but it also wrote off a loan of R60 billion, so you and I paid Eskom R83 billion to save it from itself. That is one thing not many people are willing to talk about at Eskom. We had to look into that

Commentary Two
In 2011, Deloitte reviewed the emergency coal contracts of 2008. Their report details how coal suppliers made fortunes from the crisis. Further evidence is revealed in an SIU investigation conducted in 2012. It says:

Eskom were the authors of not only their own but the country’s misfortune…

..Had the board heeded such warnings proper planning could have prevented the debacle which led to the emergency procurement of coal.

VAVI
This one, ESKOM and the banks, takes us to new, new levels

Commentary Three
Former Cosatu General secretary Zwelenzima Vavi, once part of the president’s inner circle, was so outraged, he wrote about the revelations in last Sunday’s newspaper.

Vavi
The Eskom scandal took away a few percentages of growth potential of South Africa and destroyed hundreds of workers futures

Bongani
So when the president says he is on an anti- corruption drive
Vavi
Oh no! Give me a break! Every time he says that my stomach turns. How dare does he say that when he faces 783 corruption, racketeering and money laundering charges, when he sits on an SIU report for two years. In any other democracy, the head of the state and the party that is backing him would kiss the dust, but not in SA because we have now normalized corruption.



Commentary Four
In 2015, Eskom was in trouble. Ingula, Medupi and Kusile were late and over budget, and load shedding plagued the country once again

Bongani link
With their backs against the wall, the Eskom board brought in a team of investigators led by international law firm Dentons to do a forensic fact finding enquiry, into the status of the business, and the challenges faced by the utility

Commentary five
And its this Denton’s report, withheld by Eskom, that Sikonathi Mantshantsha has revealed in his series of articles.

Sikonathi
It’s a big cover up! it’s a big cover up! The very people accused of fraud and corruption at Eskom in the Denton’s report are still working at Eskom.

Commentary Six
Dentons was only given three months to compile their report, E mails were out of bounds, they had no access to audit reports, and they could only look at documents during office hours. Energy expert Chris Yelland

Chris Yelland
Dentons made it absolutely clear that the investigation was stopped in its tracks. Now of course Eskom say that they wanted to focus on fixing Eskom and not dwelling on the past,
but you have to know what to fix, and if an investigation is stopped in its tracks you will never get to the bottom of it

Commentary seven
Sikonathi Mantshantsha meanwhile, used every opportunity he could to pester the new chairman of the board Ben Ngubane for the report

Sikonathi
I kept asking where is the report, what did the investigation find, and the answer kept changing all the time, but there was one thing he was firm on, the report was not for public consumption

Commentary eight
Eventually someone leaked him a copy. In January, he was ready to publish. Eskom went into damage control

Chris Yelland
When they realized it would be made public by the Financial mail they called a press release and said they would release it. But they didn’t!



Sikonathi
So we went there hoping to receive the report, and when we got there they changed their mind just like that.

Commentary Nine
This time Sikonathi asked Minister Lynne Brown for the report.

Up Sound Lynne Brown
The Dentons report is the boards report and while the accusation goes wild I have read the report and I think much of the report needs further investigations

Commentary ten
Shortly afterwards Eskom released a redacted version of the report

Sikonathi
I looked at it and thought I have a better report. We decided as the FM that it was in the public interest for the people of SA to understand what was killing Eskom, what cost the people of South Africa R83 billion rand

Commentary eleven
Recently the Financial Mail put the un redacted report on their website.

Sikonathi
This is the fourth version of the Dentons report, each of them progressively sanitized to the point that it can be useless, to remove any direct allegation or evidence against anyone.

Bongani Link
Nepotism, inefficiencies, the flouting of basic procurement procedures, budgets approved without knowing where the funding would coming from. It all painted a picture of an organization as the report called it, on a frolic of its own

Commentary twelve
Eskom spokesperson for the board, Khulani Qoma

Bongani
Why did Eskom try to hide the Dentons report?
Khulani
It didn’t. From the conception of the Dentons report, the intention was to use the terms of reference, to turn the business around
Bongani
With respect Eskom sat on this report for two years – we now have a redacted version of it. What do you mean you needed to fix the business first?
Khulani
Because at the time we released the report it could have resulted in some unintended consequences given the fact that we had executives gone, suspended, we had load shedding, so releasing it immediately at that time was not going to work well at least according to the thinking at the time, and the board has no regrets about that fact
Bongani
So the best option was to hide our head in the sand waiting for a better day?
Khulani
It was not to hide the report, from the first whistle there was no resolution not to release the report, it was just a question of prioritising things differently

Commentary thirteen
The bulk of Eskoms budget is spent by the primary energy division, but for Dentons getting details, was like cracking open a black box

Sikonathi
The procurement was designed to benefit the suppliers at the expense of Eskom and the suppliers were friends and family - it says people diverted opportunities away from Eskom for their own benefit.

Commentary fourteen
An example is Medupi power station. Dentons found that a supplier was selected to work on Medupi when an alternative supplier had clearly won the tender. Apparently, the selected supplier would later accept they had never done anything like this project before. Dentons says this procurement decision caused a three year delay and the inference drawn was that the supplier was a friend of senior officers

Khulani Qomo
The biggest issue is procurement. We are getting a lot of flak perception that we are not doing anything. We have done quite a lot of work to rejig the procurement, we have changed the operating model, we have changed the structure and created the checks and balances …and the independent firms externally

Commentary fifteen
In 2015 Eskom was spending a billion rand a month on diesel just keep the lights on. Questionable suppliers became overnight millionaires. But in the final report no one is directly implicated. Those details, alleges Sikonathi, were removed early on

Sikonathi
It had specific allegations against specific people so when Dentons made that presentation the board didn’t like it. The board then formally resolved to destroy those allegations against people, and to recall those copies of that presentation

Commentary Sixteen
Eskom says Mantshantsha’s stories are based on the contents of an uncorroborated draft report, but even this final report says that some senior executives ran Eskom through certain well placed proxies. Dentons record they needed more time to corroborate the allegations.


Bongani to Khulani
Why did the board issue instruction for information to be destroyed?
Khulani
Had that report leaked out before it was firmed up it would have result in various other things that we did not intend at the time
Bongani
But you certainly cannot say its standard practice for the board to destroy the information once its uncovered
Khulani
It was not destroying information it was destroying the availability of information in the hands of people who shouldn’t have it.

Commentary seventeen
Eskom says that they have implemented 13 out of 18 of the Denton recommendations. But, the man who has been tasked to take Eskom forward is interim CEO Matshela Koko, caught lying on camera last year about the Gupta coal contract

THE END duration: 10 21

Promo One
Shocking new revelations into Eskom revealed
Vavi
This one, ESKOM and the banks, takes us to new, new levels

Promo Two 15 seconds
For two years Eskom refused to make a report into what went wrong at the utility available to the public
Sikonathi
I kept asking where is the report? What did the investigation find?

Promo Three
Sikonathi
It’s a big cover up! it’s a big cover up!
Commentary
Has Eskom tried to hide evidence of malfeasance at senior management level. They say no.
Bongani
Why did Eskom try to hide the Dentons report from the public?
Khulani
It didn’t.
